title: Optimizely Web Experimentation signup-flow flaw abused to inject skimmer, wallet swapper and iOS exploit kits into 178 organizations' scripts (OPTIMJACK)
why: Optimizely confirmed an attacker exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to write malicious JavaScript into customer projects; Report URI (Scott Helme) found 188 infected snippets for 178 organizations on Nov 16 (Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, HSBC and others), confirmed by BleepingComputer and The Hacker News. It is a hosted-service flaw with no CVE, so it cannot be in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance for it. Nov 17: Optimizely's status notice confirms an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and says it is fixed. Hudson Rock and researcher Kirk of Ohey traced the same loader in Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly responses as early as Nov 13 (Help Net Security, infostealers.com). Still no CVE, and nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Nov 18: Optimizely's statement to Gizmodo/ABC confirms the signup-flow exploit and the fix; Zoom disabled Optimizely in production. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: If you use Optimizely Web, review every project's Project JavaScript and experiment custom code for script you did not write (Report URI's checklist), rotate Optimizely users/API tokens, treat card data and non-HttpOnly cookies from Nov 16 pages as exposed, and push iOS/iPadOS to 18.7.3+ or 26.3+.
product: Optimizely Web Experimentation (hosted snippet / Project JavaScript); downstream iOS/iPadOS older than 18.7.3 / 26.3 targeted by the delivered kits

title: Apache Roller XML-RPC pre-auth Java deserialization RCE (4.0.0-6.1.4), Apache says actively exploited
why: Apache's Nov 17 advisory for CVE-2026-129448 says the flaw 'is being actively exploited'. It widens the September CVE-2026-82384 (6.1.5 only) back to 4.0.0, so scanners keyed on the old record miss older installs. Public PoCs for 82384 exist on GitHub and Sploitus. SecurityOnline reports it is not in CISA KEV, and CISA's last KEV additions were on Nov 13. Microsoft has published nothing on it. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Roller to 6.1.6 or later. Until then, set enabledForExtensions=false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart, then check that host for unexpected JVM child processes.
product: Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 (fixed in 6.1.6)

title: Java4Shell: OpenJDK AVX-512 Base64 decoder heap overflow enabling pre-auth RCE in Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and others
why: Calif disclosed Java4Shell on Nov 17 and published a memory-corruption reproducer. It says it got pre-auth RCE on default Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, but has not released those exploits. Oracle fixed it in the Nov 17 CSPU (CVSS 3.1 8.1; Calif rates it CVSS 4.0 9.2), and Horizon3, Rapid7, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and oss-security cover it. Reports say the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK is affected, but as of Nov 18 Microsoft had not published a fixed build and MSRC has no advisory. It is not in CISA KEV. watchTowr and Upwind report no exploitation in the wild yet.
action: Update Java runtimes to the Nov 17 fixed builds (Oracle/Amazon out; for Temurin, Zulu, Microsoft and Red Hat, watch for their builds). Until then, start the JVMs behind Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, or -XX:UseAVX=2.
product: OpenJDK-based Java runtimes 17.0.6 and later (Java 17, 21, 25, 27; Oracle Java 8 Performance Pack) on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI

title: Perforce Puppet Enterprise report-processing deserialization RCE on Puppet Server, added to CISA KEV Nov 17
why: Not ahead: CISA added it to KEV on Nov 17 (federal due date Dec 1).
action: Upgrade Puppet Enterprise/Puppet Server to the fixed release, disable or restrict autosigning, and review Puppet Server for unexpected child processes and recent changes to the catalog or modules.
product: Puppet Enterprise / Puppet Server (report processing)

title: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts push a CI secret stealer; secrets taken from 1,800+ repos, with AWS and Entra ID persistence
why: Aikido, OX Security, SafeDep and StepSecurity report a live campaign since Nov 10: stolen tokens for 4,837 GitHub accounts opened ~62-66k probe PRs and the stealer ran in at least 1,806 repositories, still ongoing on Nov 12 with exfil moved to Telegram. The payload adds wfx-ci-* federated credentials to Entra ID apps and rewrites AWS role trust policies, which survive secret rotation. There is no CVE (no product bug), so no CISA KEV entry, and no Microsoft or GitHub guidance appeared in the sources reviewed. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Search your GitHub org for PRs titled "docs: dependency audit notes" or wfx-docs branches since Nov 10; for any hit revoke that account's tokens and rotate every secret its workflows could reach, then hunt Entra ID for federated credentials named wfx-ci-* and AWS sessions named wfx-*.
vendor: GitHub (abuse of stolen developer tokens; no product flaw)
product: GitHub Actions workflows and npm postinstall hooks in any repository a compromised account can write to (since Nov 10, 2026)

title: WP Duplicate (LocalSync) WordPress plugin <=1.1.11: unauthenticated file upload to RCE, exploited, no patch
why: WPScan, the CNA, says the flaw is being actively exploited in the wild. A public exploit (Duplicate2Shell) was indexed on Sploitus and Vulners on Nov 15, and SecurityOnline reports that no patch exists. Microsoft has no advisory, and the flaw is not in CISA KEV, whose last additions were on Nov 13. WPScan has not published attack volumes or IOCs. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Deactivate and delete WP Duplicate from every WordPress site. Then look in wp-content/uploads and the plugin directories for PHP files you did not put there, and rotate admin credentials if you find any.
product: WP Duplicate WordPress plugin through 1.1.11 (no fixed release)

title: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI releases 1.26.1/1.26.2 hijacked with Azure/GitHub Actions credential stealer
why: On Nov 17 two malicious releases of Microsoft's official agent-framework package (about 192k downloads a month) were uploaded outside its release pipeline. Each installs a .pth hook that steals Azure, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions and CI credentials on every Python start. Socket, OX Security, SafeDep, Aikido, Wiz and others reported it (The Hacker News, OTX). PyPI quarantined both versions. I found no MSRC advisory, Microsoft statement or Defender guidance. A public GitHub issue says it is unconfirmed whether the upload credential has been revoked. As a supply-chain incident with no CVE, it cannot be in CISA KEV.
action: Search lockfiles, pip/uv caches, CI caches and internal mirrors for agent-framework 1.26.1/1.26.2. Pin 1.26.0, rebuild affected hosts from clean images, and rotate every Azure, GitHub and cloud credential reachable from them, including OIDC trust for GitHub Actions jobs that ran with id-token: write.
product: agent-framework (PyPI) 1.26.1 and 1.26.2

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6460 type confusion: low-privileged database user to OS code execution, RCE technique now public
why: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a write-up turning the 22-year-old type confusion into code execution, and an independent researcher reproduced the crash with four SQL statements as a zero-privilege role (dev.to); the item hit Hacker News today. OffSeq and SecurityOnline report no exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Hosted PostgreSQL services may be exposed, but no cloud-provider statement was found. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 (14 is now end-of-life), prioritising multi-tenant servers, and until then remove CREATE privileges from untrusted roles.
product: PostgreSQL before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 (part of a 52-CVE release on Nov 12, 2026)

title: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 hosts exploited to deploy XMRig at 13 organizations (likely known unauthenticated WebCam Server RCE)
why: Huntress SOC saw attackers abuse internet-exposed GeoVision GV-VMS at 13 organizations (most activity Nov 8-10): commands spawned by GeoStartupAgentService.exe as SYSTEM, a BYOVD driver and IFEO hijacks to disable Microsoft Defender, then a DHT/PKARR Go loader and XMRig. Huntress told Help Net Security (Nov 16) that the sampled hosts ran GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 and that one of three unauthenticated RCEs in GeoVision's April 2026 advisory is the most likely entry point, but the exact CVE is not confirmed. No CVE for this activity is in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft guidance; the campaign actively tries to switch Defender off. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade GV-VMS to V17.4.8.58 or later, take GeoVision management interfaces off the internet (VPN/IP allowlist), and hunt for cmd/PowerShell children of GeoStartupAgentService.exe and IFEO Debugger keys on Defender processes.
product: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 (older than fixed V17.4.8.58)

title: SAPBleed / ICM2SHELL: pre-auth WebSocket heap overflow in SAP ICM, Web Dispatcher and HANA XS (memory leak of SSO tickets and TLS keys, RCE)
why: nullFaktor published full technical details and a demo video on Full Disclosure on Nov 17. Without credentials, it read arbitrary ICM memory, pulled the server's TLS private key and a valid MYSAPSSO2 SSO ticket, and demonstrated RCE. Onapsis gave SAP a working exploit. SAP patched it on Nov 10 (CVSS 10.0). No exploit code is public and no exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has no advisory or Defender coverage for it.
action: Apply SAP Security Notes 3778530 (ICM kernel/dw.sar) and 3778556 (Web Dispatcher and HANA XS). Until patched, block WebSocket upgrades at the Web Dispatcher. After patching, rotate the TLS keys and invalidate SSO tickets on exposed systems.
product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP ICM, SAP Web Dispatcher, SAP HANA XS internal Web Dispatcher (see SAP Notes 3778530, 3778556)

title: Apache Shiro DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled (CVE-2026-129349)
why: Apache disclosed it on oss-security on Nov 13 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, network, no privileges). It is a Java library, not a Microsoft product, and it is not in CISA KEV. No public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Find Java apps that bundle shiro-core with an LDAP realm and upgrade them to 3.0.2. Until then, turn off authentication caching on those realms.
product: Apache Shiro (shiro-core) before 3.0.1

title: Apache APISIX 3.20.0 fixes 7 flaws, incl. unauthenticated route-auth bypass (CVE-2026-124680) and identity-header spoofing (CVE-2026-124679)
why: Apache posted seven APISIX advisories on oss-security on Nov 13. Two let unauthenticated clients get past authentication in certain configurations. Not a Microsoft product, not in CISA KEV, and no public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade APISIX gateways to 3.20.0. Until then, check for routes without auth that share an upstream with protected routes, and turn off forward-auth allow_degradation.
product: Apache APISIX 0.9 through 3.19.0 (124680); 3.18.0 through 3.19.0 (124679)

title: Cyrus SASL SRP mechanism authentication bypass: A=N forces zero shared secret (CVE-2026-129483)
why: VulnCheck (CNA) published it Nov 15 with an upstream fix commit and oss-security post; CVSS 9.1/9.3, network, no privileges. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV. Only servers that enable the SRP SASL mechanism are exposed. A Microsoft CSAF/VEX record exists for the package, but no Microsoft product guidance. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Check whether any service offers the SRP SASL mechanism (mech_list / installed libsrp plugin) and disable or remove the SRP plugin until distro packages carry upstream commit fb3724f.
product: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 (SRP server mechanism)

title: Arize Phoenix unauthenticated applyChatTemplate format-string flaw leaks PHOENIX_SECRET, enabling admin session forgery (CVSS 10.0)
why: GitHub advisory GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3 and the CVE record (published Nov 16) describe an endpoint that is unauthenticated on default installs and exposes PHOENIX_SECRET, allowing admin session-token forgery. No public exploit or in-the-wild use reported; not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft coverage. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Phoenix to 15.7.0 or later, keep it off the public internet, and rotate PHOENIX_SECRET and any credentials in its environment if it was exposed.
product: Phoenix AI observability platform 13.0.0 to before 15.7.0

title: Oracle Nov 2026 CSPU: unauthenticated CVSS 9.8-10.0 flaws in Access Manager, WebLogic, Platform Security for Java, BI EE, E-Business Suite
why: Oracle's Nov 17 CSPU (655 fixes) includes several flaws an unauthenticated attacker can reach over HTTP or SOAP: Access Manager auth engine 91500 and 91510 (10.0, scope change), WebLogic takeover 91456 and 91470 (9.8), Platform Security for Java 114824 (10.0), and EBS 114924 and 114925 (9.8). These product lines have a history of fast weaponization. VulDB lists no public exploit yet. None is in CISA KEV, and Microsoft has no advisory or detection guidance for them.
action: Patch internet-facing Oracle Access Manager and WebLogic first. Until then, restrict the WebLogic T3/IIOP/SOAP and OAM admin/auth endpoints to trusted networks.

title: NoisyTCP: Linux kernel TCP pre-auth remote crash (CVE-2026-99288), present since 4.4, full details public after embargo
why: Hyunwoo Kim posted the full NoisyTCP write-up to oss-security on Nov 15 once the linux-distros embargo ended. A remote attacker with no login can panic any Linux host that has a TCP listener and spreads packets over 2+ RX queues or RPS (default on most cloud VMs). Kim has a private lab PoC (5 s to 2 min against KVM guests), but no exploit code is public and nobody has reported attacks. Debian and Oracle UEK have fixed kernels. As of Nov 15-16, Ubuntu and RHEL/Rocky/Alma had no fix yet. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft/MSRC (Azure Linux) entry in the collected data. Scored low because the impact is DoS only: Red Hat 7.5, no NVD score. Nov 16 update: BleepingComputer and others now cover it; Debian and Arch ship fixed kernels, Ubuntu and RHEL trackers still list it as unfixed/affected; researcher has still not published exploit code and no attacks are reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Patch internet-facing Linux hosts to a kernel with commit 4e2b3ef19e0e (6.12.117/6.18.63/7.3.4 or your distro backport) and reboot. Until a distro fix ships, Ubuntu/RHEL hosts can set net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=0 in every netns, or use a single RX queue with RPS/RFS off. Weigh the SYN-flood trade-off first.
product: Linux kernel 4.4 through 6.12.116, 6.13-6.18.62, 6.19-7.3.3 (TCP established-socket lookup); EOL 7.2 gets no fix

title: 'Hello Again': fTPM lockout rollback via RPMC flaws lets attackers with physical access brute-force Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN
why: Academic paper (arXiv 2611.18126, CCS '26, Nov 13) demonstrates end-to-end on locked hardware: a 4-digit Hello PIN in 40 hours, BitLocker 6-digit TPM+PIN worst case 20 days, by rolling back fTPM anti-hammering state (Winbond RPMC HMAC key leak via glitching; AMD controller not verifying increments; some AMD boards with no rollback protection). Per the authors, no vendor committed to a root-cause fix; Microsoft only raised its recommended minimum Hello PIN to 6 digits. No CVE, no MSRC advisory. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: For lost/stolen-device risk, enforce Windows Hello and BitLocker pre-boot PINs of at least 6 (preferably 8+) digits or alphanumeric PINs via policy.
product: Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN on x86 systems using firmware TPMs (AMD, Intel, Pluton) backed by SPI flash

title: needrestart local root via forged session cgroup and notify-send hook (Debian/Ubuntu)
why: On Nov 17 the researcher posted a full public write-up to oss-security after the linux-distros embargo. FOSS Linux reports Canonical marks all supported Ubuntu releases vulnerable with no fixed version, and neither Debian nor Canonical had a fix that evening. It is not in KEV, and Microsoft (Defender for Linux) has published nothing on it. No exploitation has been reported.
action: Until distro fixes land, disable the needrestart apt hook (or set it to list-only mode) on multi-user Debian/Ubuntu hosts, then upgrade needrestart once the patched package is published.
product: needrestart 3.6 (Debian bookworm 3.6-4+deb12u3, Ubuntu 24.04 3.6-7ubuntu4.5); Debian trixie 3.11-1 partly

title: Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE Station Launcher App: unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) plus two command injections
why: Vendor (3DS CNA) advisories published Nov 16: CVE-2026-93664 unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-77033/19732 OS command injection. No public exploit or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 18 09Z: the only CISA KEV addition since Nov 13 is Puppet CVE-2026-115731, so this is still not in KEV.
action: Apply the fix packs named in the 3DS advisories for CVE-2026-93664/77033/19732 and restrict network access to Station Launcher services.
product: 3DEXPERIENCE platform Station Launcher App, R2023x through R2026x

title: Telegram for Android: NebuSec claims two RCE bypasses of the new bot-widget sandbox (no CVE, no fix confirmed)
why: NebuSec published a write-up and demo videos (Nov 14-17, reported by The Hacker News) showing two ways for a malicious bot widget to run code outside the seccomp filter Telegram added last week. The demos ran on a test server, and only approved bots can send widgets in production. Telegram has not confirmed a fix. There is no CVE or KEV entry, and Microsoft has no coverage. These are unverified vendor claims.
action: Keep Telegram for Android updated, and tell mobile users not to start or interact with widgets from unknown bots until Telegram confirms a fix.
product: Telegram for Android (widget sandbox, demo on 13.2.2 (7303))
